title: Victor Charles Mayer and Catherine Earle Mayer
description:
This is Victor Charles Mayer and Catherine Earle Mayer ... probably at the Devon Horse Show or hunting with the Brandywine Hounds.  Note that grandfather is carrying a hound whip and wearing a Whip Cap signifying he was a Gentleman Whip or Master of Fox Hounds.  Other men wore silk top hats similar to Catherine's.  Sidesaddle for ladies was customary.  Few ladies dares to ride astride until the 1930s and 1940s. 

As you no doubt know your Great Great Grandfather, Charles Elmer Mayer, Victor's father, bought a thousand acres adjacent to Lenape near West Chester, on the Brandywine Creek in 1895 and moved his Hounds from the Kennels at his great house in Haverford "Avonwood Court" on Rose Lane in Haverford, to Brandywine Farms in 1903.  Brandy Hounds was a private pack (not a club, like Radnor) "by invitation only" until 2004 when your cousin , Jane Mather Sullivan, shut it down due to urban spawl. 

When Charles died, Victor's younger brother, Gilbert, and he became joint masters.  They changed Charles English foxhounds and developed a breed of American foxhounds which have consistently won best of breed in the US and whose descendants may be found in almost every American pack.  

Victor won the Maryland Hunt Cup once, and Gilbert won it twice.

Remembrance of Edward Wharton Shober jr.

title: Bridge Abutments on Chester Valley Trail (ex Chester Valley Railroad)
description: I walked the Chester Valley Trail yesterday between Contention Lane to Devon Alley Forge Rd.  First time I had ever been in there.    I came upon an old pair of bridge abutments, behind at about where the McDonald’s on Swedesford Rd is.   I took these two photos looking east at about 4 PM.  The abutment on the right (the second, brighter photo) is more elaborate, with wider wing walls and appears to have an ornamental column on the east side, where even today, there is a stone-paved walkway up to it with signs of use. I didn’t go up there to explore. - Jim Brazel
rights: Owned by Jim Brazel
subject: Railroad

title: Tom Nelson
description:
On South Leopard Road, across from where we lived was Doctor Thomas Nelson, who had a large estate.  They had a son Thomas who was a mothers boy ... and he was not allowed to talk or play with us kids.  He also had a pony, named Major, white, which he would ride down to the road.  We had a tennis court and he would like to come down and try to play .. he was very friendly at that point.  When he got older and got a car he would drive by our house with head in the air and makeout like he never saw us .. speak or wave.  When he got married his wife as also like that.

George Moran, 1987

title: Duffy’s Cut enclosure
description:
This enclosure was built at the purported / believed gravesite of the Irish immigrant laborers who died en masse during the construction of "Duffy’s Cut" on the Philadelphia & Columbia in the early 1830s.
  
It is located on the south side of the ROW, just west of where Sugartown Road formerly crossed the P&C and later the PRR.  There is a PA state marker at King St. & Sugartown Rd. commemorating the tragedy.
 
This enclosure was built in 1909 when Martin Clement of PRR management investigated the site. He later (1935-48) became  president of the PRR.  It is substantially built out of salvaged stone sleeper blocks from the original P&C Railroad. Note the drilled holes for spiking the rail to the block. 

The generally accepted number of fatalities is fifty-seven and recently, human remains have been found.
rights: Owned by the Tredyffrin Easttown Historical Society
subject: House
refs: See Duffy’s Cut Project

title: Pickering Creek Farm
description:
This "AIRGRAPH" photo taken by Aero Service Group, Philadelphia, has been copied from the collection of Edward Ludwick, Jr. of Gladwyne PA.  It shows the property "Pickering Creek Farm" of his grandfather, George Priestly, on Valley Park Road in Schuylkill Township, looking east towards Valley Forge.

Mr. Ludwick’s father, Edward Ludwick, Sr., had the architect’s commission to perform a modernization of the property in the early 1920s, after his father in law had purchased it.  Mr. Ludwick recalls that extensive modernization and stonework were done on the main house and that the main barn and entrance driveway were also modernized.  His mother, Bessie Priestley Ludwick, remembered the Phoenixville, Valley Forge, and Strafford railway trolley going by in the early 1920s.  The tracks and poles for the trolley line are visible in the bottom of the photo, on the south side of Valley Park Road.

Written by J. Brazel from interview with Edward Ludwick, Jr., 30 December 2014.
rights: owned by Tredyffrin Easttown Historical Society

description:
On back of postcard, dated 6/24/1973

Built prior to 1736, it was the homestead of a 50 acre farm called Nant ye Ewig (tumbling brook).  Property was conveyed to the church by Henry Davis. 

The Rev. David Jones and his wife Ann and 4 children Eleanor,12; May,8; Margen(?), 4, David, 1 occupied the house in March 19, 1776.

The present owners of the Parsonage are Mr & Mrs R. W. Rauch.  Other owners Lester & Lucressa Morris, Jonh Ebenenzeller, Mr & Mrs David Echel.

title: St Norberts Church
comment: In 1956 Cardinal O’Hara, then Archbishop of Philadelphia, formed a new parish, St. Norbert, from portions of St. Monica’s in Berwyn and St. Patrick’s in Malvern. He entrusted its care to the Norbertines. The pastor of St. Norbert Parish is nominated by the Abbot of Daylesford Abbey. The founding pastor of the parish was Father Robert L. Hyde. He celebrated the first parish Mass at 7:00 AM on Sunday, July 15, 1956 in the old Paoli Fire House. - Roger Thorne

title: Original South Porch, Hillcrest
comment: Mary A. Bair House – also known as Hillcrest, or the Hunter-Bair House – Conestoga Road & Cassatt Avenue, Berwyn, Pennsylvania. Built circa-1887, it is attributed to architect Allen Evans of Furness & Evans. William Drennan sold the 14-acre estate to Edmund A. W. Hunter in 1892. It was bought by funeral director Oliver Bair in 1905, and Bair's daughter occupied it until the 1950s. Situated atop a hill overlooking the Great Valley, the house originally had a 3-story front porch crowned by a dome. - unknown contributor to Wikimedia Commons

title: Ximena Wells Burns
description: William H Burns was married to the pastors niece, the former Ximena Wells (1862-1894). Both of them were musical and participated frequently in local music events at Trinity Presbyterian Church in Berwyn. They had six children at the time the new church was being built; two years later Ximena Burns died at age 32 giving birth to their seventh child. title: Cleaver’s Store
description: Caption: I. A. Cleaver’s general store in Berwyn about 1900. Berwyn, like other towns along the Main Line, was initially established along the old Lancaster Turnpike and Conestoga Road used by thousands of travelers throughout the eighteenth century as the main road westward.  By the late nineteenth century, businesses such as Cleaver’s often continued to serve the new settlements spurred on by the growth and success of the railroads.

title: Devon Inn
description: Caption: The Devon Inn, inspired by the quick success of the Bryn Mawr Hotel, was built in an effort to appeal to Philadelphias wealthiest citizens as a summer resort.  After the first building was destroyed less than a year after its completion, the inn seen here was built, in 1884.  The Devon Horse Show was conceived and initially held on the grounds of the inn in 1896.  The building was later acquired by the Valley Forge Military Academy in 1928.  As before, less than a year after it changed hands, the inn was destroyed by fire.

title: President Calvin Coolidge at the Devon Horse Show
description: Caption: President Calvin Coolidge (at center) with his wife and several members of the Main Line community are shown attending the Devon Horse Show on May 30, 1922.  First held in 1896, the Devon Horse Show is the oldest and largest outdoor multi-breed horse show in the nation. Original interest in establishing the show grew from the important role of horses in transportation as the number of large estates multiplied along the railroad line. The horse show continues to emphasize good horse breeding and training, as it did when founded.

title: Diamond Rock School
description: Caption: Located near Paoli, the Diamond Rock Octagonal School built in 1818 by Mennonites as a one-room schoolhouse.  The eight sides accommodated all six grade levels, a teacher’s wall, and the door.  The teacher stood in the center of the room to address each class.  The school was restored in 1908 and is seen here in 1955.  It remains a popular summertime historic attraction.

title: Strafford train station
description: Caption: The Strafford train station as it appeared in 1964. The buildings interesting history begins at the 1876 Centennial Exposition held in Fairmount Park, where it was likely used as a catalog sales shed. It was purchased by the Pennsylvania Railroad and moved to the Wayne station. In the late 1880s, it was moved for the last time to Strafford, where it remains today. - this history has been debunked by Greg Prichard debunked in the following article: Strafford Station at the Centennial: Fact or Fiction?

title: Upper Forge Excavation
description: “Potts-Dewees Forge.  The long lost Valley (originally Mount Joy) Forge. Due to the silting of Valley Creek, the site of the forge had been lost for over a century.  Having being rediscovered in 1929, it was dug out from over 11 feet of slit.  This was the forge belonging to Isaac Potts and William Dewees, that was burnt by the British, September 18, 1777. The forge stood between Mount Joy and Valley Forge Mountain. The photograph shows the north wall during excavation. The building was constructed of stone without mortar binding.”

title: Betzwood
description: “In the midst of a region known for its splendid tillage and beautiful vistas, Betzwood, upon the eastern shore of the Schuylkill River, opposite Port Kennedy and within sight of Valley Forge, is the most extensive and beautiful farm property. This fine tract of more than a thousand acres has been developed by Mr. John F. Betz of Philadelphia, as not only a ideal country home for himself and Mr. John F. Betz jr., but as a stock farm for the breeding of fine cattle and horses. Mr. Betz also engages here in raising of carriage, saddle, and draught horses of registered pedigrees. Betzwood includes besides its broad grazing acres, extensive well planted lawns, threaded with winding private drives, handsome modern residences, conservatories, a deer park and large power plant on the banks of the river. Betzwood station, upon the Schuylkill division of the Pennsylvania Railroad, also upon the property, is reached by frequent trains in about one hour from Broad Street station. Mr. Buck Taylor the famous frontiersman, is superintendent.” - from Valley Forge: A Chronicle of American Heroism by Frank Taylor (1905)

photographer: J. Lawrence Dixon, Quaker City Railroad Society
title: Beans Mineral Railway Cars
contributor: James P. Brazel, West Jersey Chapter, National Railway Historical Society
description:
View of three abandoned, partially salvaged wooden body gondola/dumper style cars at the disused Beans Quarry And Sand Company narrow gauge railroad terminal yard at the Company’s rock crusher in Valley Forge Village.
This rear view shows the car end, link and pin type coupler and the side drop doors of these cars which brought quartzite rock and sand down from the Bean Sand And Quarry Company’s quarries on Mt. Misery to the company’s rock crusher for processing and shipment via a siding on the Reading Railroad. One of the car’s trucks is visible under the rear end of the closest car.  The horizontal style handbrake application wheels at the far ends of the two more distant cars are visible in this photo. - Jim Brazel
rights: Owned by the Tredyffrin Easttown Historical Society
subject: Railroad
refs: Sand, Railways, and Movies; the Bean Sand Business, TEHS Quarterly, vol. 43, #4 (Fall 2006)

photographer: J. Lawrence Dixon, Quaker City Railroad Society
title: Bean Mineral Railway Locomotive
contributor: James P. Brazel, West Jersey Chapter, National Railway Historical Society
description:
Front/right quarter view of abandoned Climax Class B geared logging locomotive at the disused Beans Quarry And Sand Company narrow gauge railroad terminal yard at the Company’s rock crusher in Valley Forge Village.  At right of the photo the engine and car service facility’s water tank for supply to the steam locomotive’s water tank has been overturned from its concrete elevated foundation. 
The headlamp, round front smokebox door and most of the sheet metal sheathing on the boiler have been removed since active use. 
A photo and information on a similar Climax Class B locomotive in operating order may be found at TEHS Image Collection Identifier RR02, SN 1175.  
Research on the Climax Manufacturing Company’s production and sales indicates that a Class B locomotive of 40 tons weight was sold to Beans Sand And Quarry Company in or before the year 1915. Ref.: The Climax Locomotive, D.B. Thompson et al, 2002 Oso Publishing
. - Jim Brazel

title: Bryn Mawr Homes
description:
Strafford Village Architectural Design Album.

This collection documents the architectural vision of the Strafford Village development located northeast of Strafford train station in Tredyffrin Township. Builder Stephan Schifter started the development in 1939 and built several homes before the start of World War II, continuing construction at the war”s conclusion. The designs of these homes are represented in the pages in this scrapbook and other loose drawings prepared by architect Harold Edward Williams. The homes depicted are examples of the revivalist styles popular in the pre-war era and include designs inspired by English, French, and Early American architecture. The documents consist of of a total of 58 sheets of plans and renderings, and one overall plot plan of the development pasted to the inside cover of the disassembled scrapbook. - Greg Prichard
rights: Owned by Tredyffrin Easttown Historical Society.
subject: House
refs: Strafford Village by Stephan C. Schifter, TEHS Quarterly, vol 41, #1 (Winter 2004)

title: Devon Design Center
comment:
Devon Design Center was originally part of the Devon Horse Show grounds. For many years, the building was occupied as an antique shop with dirt floors and horse stalls still visible within the showroom.

Since the mid-80s the building has been transformed into an impressive design center featuring complementary retailers of home interior furnishings, accents, flooring, tiles and even antiques.

The original beams are still visible on the second floor as are the mechanisms for the hand-operated elevator that was used to lift the surreys from the ground floor below.

comment: I don't think the track material in this picture between the main tracks and the river are an indication of preparations for laying a third track. It is hard to see, but there is a white-painted tool house in the middle of this track material.  This is actually a rare scene to be able to see a local material storage yard in the 1870s. - Rick Bates

title: Franklin Burns at Hawk Mountain
description: My dad was an ornithologist by avocation.  His interest in birding started when he was a pre-teen.  His interest grew over the years and he was a member of several ornithological societies.  I believe he was a member of the Wilson Ornithological Society.  He may have met Frank Burns through the Wilson.  I don’t know.  Dad was a frequent visitor to the Hawk Mountain Sanctuary and knew the curator there, Maurice Broun and dad used to do a lot of birding with another amateur ornithologist, Albert Conway.  Dad also banded birds and was issued a permit by the State of Pennsylvania.  All of these associations are possible links to how dad knew Burns but he did say that he had been on birding excursions with him. I’ve attached a photo from the collection of negatives that dad had.  It was marked as Frank L. Burns, Hawk Mtn., Sept. 1942.  I really can’t tell you any more with any certainty.

title: The Justice Bell, Valley Forge National Historical Park, 1915
comment: HCS 3/14/2023. Original image located at this link.
description: Exact photo date unknown. On June 15, 1915 the Justice Bell began its whistle stop tour of Pennsylvania in support of a proposed amendment to the Pennsylvania State Constitution giving women the right to vote. The tour covered more than 5,000 miles in less than six months and crisscrossed the state visiting all sixty-seven counties! Women in Pennsylvania finally gained the right to vote on September 25, 1920, a month after the ratification of the 19th Amendment. You can view the Justice Bell in the Veteran's Hall at Washington's Memorial Chapel located in Valley Forge NHP. Image courtesy of the Pennsylvania League of Women Voters.

title: President Nixon visit Valley Forge Memorial Arch
comment: HCS 3/15/2023. Original image located at this link.
description: Boy Scouts of America National Jamborees are quadrennial gatherings of thousands of scouts from around the country and the world. The first was held in 1935 in Washington, DC. With the advent of World War II, however, these huge events were deferred for the duration of the war. In the late 1940s, the Cold War commenced-an unsettling period of repeated crises and tensions between former allies the United States and the Soviet Union. For reassurance, citizens looked back to the founding ideals of democracy, and interest in sites and stories of the American Revolution was strong. When the Boy Scouts of America decided to reestablish jamborees, they chose Valley Forge, the icon of the American Revolution. Valley Forge served as the site of three National Jamborees, in 1950, 1957, and 1964.

In the late 1940s, the Cold War commenced-an unsettling period of repeated crises and tensions between former allies the United States and the Soviet Union. For reassurance, citizens looked back to the founding ideals of democracy, and interest in sites and stories of the American Revolution was strong. When the Boy Scouts of America decided to reestablish jamborees, they chose Valley Forge, the icon of the American Revolution. Valley Forge served as the site of three National Jamborees, in 1950, 1957, and 1964.

title: National Memorial Arch, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: North Elevation To the officers and private soldiers of the Continental Army December 19, 1777 June 19, 1778 Erected by the authority of the 61st Act of Congress June 25, 1910 South Elevation "Naked and starving as they are we cannot enough admireincomparable patience and fidelity of the soldiery" Washington at Valley Forge February 16, 1778 "They shall hunger no more neither thirst anymore" Revelations Inside East And here in this place of sacrifice in this vale of humiliation in this valley of the shadow of that death out of which the life of America rose regenerate and free let us believe with an abiding Faith that to them Union will seem as dear and liberty as sweet and progress as glorious as they were to our fathers and are to you and me and that the institutions which have made us happy preserved by the virtue of our children shall bless the remotest generation of the time to come. Henry Armitt Brown Inside West Commander in Chief George Washington Major Generals DeKalb Greene Lafayette Lee Mifflin Steuben Stirling Sullivan Brigadier Generals Armstrong DuPortail Glover Huntington Knox Learned McIntosh Maxwell Muhlenberg Patterson Poor Scott Smallwood Varnum Wayne Weedon Woodford Pulaski DESCRIPTION: Granite with bronze plaques and carved decorations. DONOR & DATE: Designed by Paul P. Cret; erected by the U.S.-Government June 25, 1910; transferred to the custody of the Common wealth of Pennsylvania by Hon. Champ Clark, Speaker of the House, June 19, 1917. HISTORICAL DATA: Being a simplified version of the Triumphal Arch of Titus in Rome (AD81) which marked the capture of Jerusalem by Titus in, AD70, Marks the entrance of the Continental Army into the Valley Forge encampment.

title: Weedon’s Brigade Marker, Valley Forge Park
description: Brigade Marker Weedon’s Brigade Continental Army - Valley Forge December 19, 1777 June 19, 1778 Greene’s Division Major General Nathaniel Greene Weedon’s Brigade Brigadier General George Weedon Commanding 13th Regiment Infantry Pennsylvania Line Col. Walter Stewart Raised as State Regiment of Foot March 1, 1777, attached to Pennsylvania Line as 13th Regiment Infantry Nov. 12, 1777 - consolidated with the 2nd Regiment Infantry July 1, 1778 2nd Regiment Virginia Infantry Lieut. Col. Charles Dabney 6th Regiment Virginia Infantry Col; John Gibson 10th Regiment Virginia Infantry Col. John Green 14th Regiment Virginia Infantry Lieut. Col. William Davis DESCRIPTION: Granite with bronze plaque 6’ x 4’ x 2’ DONOR & DATE: The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA: Fourteen complete Virginia Regiments wintered at Valley Forge with more units arriving early in 1778. General George Weedon of Virginia commanded five of these regiments.

title: Anthony Wayne statute, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: East Face Anthony Wayne Colonel Chester Co. Battalion of Minute Men July 21 1775 Colonel 4th Penna. Infantry Battalion January 3, 1776 Brig. General Continental Army February 21, 1777 to November 3, 1778 Brevetted Major General September 30, 1783 Resolved unanimously, that the thanks of Congress be presented to Brig. General Wayne for his brave, prudent and soldierly conduct in the spirited and well-conducted attack on Stony Point that a gold medal emblematical of this action be struck and presented to Brig. General Wayne Major General and Commander-in-Chief United States Army, March 5, 1792 to December 15, 1796 West Face Chairman of the Chester County Committee 1774 Deputy to the Provincial Convention 1774 Member of the Assembly 1774, 1784-1785 Delegate to the Provincial Convention 1775 Member of the Committee of Safety 1775-1776 Member of the Council of Censors 1783 Member of the Pennsylvania Convention to, ratify the Constitution 1787. Born in Chester Co, Pennsylvania January 1 1745 Died at Presqu isle, Pennsylvania December 15 1796 North Face South Face Virtue Liberty and Independence Erected by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania Lead me forward Wayne at Stony Point DESCRIPTION: Bronze statue with Missouri red granite base. DONOR & DATE - Henry K. Bush-Brown, Sculptor; authorized by the 1905 Legislature of Pennsylvania, unveiled guest orator, the Hon. Samuel W. Pennypacker, June 20, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA: The first monument to be erected by the state of Pennsylvania in Valley Forge National Historical Park and is a replica of the one commissioned for Stoney Point, New York. The site was chosen because of its location within the area of the Pennsylvania line and it is said to be in view of General Waynes Headquarters located nearby.

comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Memorial Marker-George Washington and Troops These trees are dedicated to George Washington and his troops who suffered and died during the winter of 1777 Donated by the survivors of the attack on Pearl Harbor Dedicated December 7, 1977 DESCRIPTION - Gray granite 22 x 13 with an 18 x 12 bronze plaque. DONOR & DATE - Pearl Harbor Survivors Association, December 7, 1977. HISTORICAL DATA - This marker was dedicated on the 36th anniversary of, the attack on Pearl Harbor by the Japanese during World War II.

title: Virgina State Marker, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Virginia This marker is placed at the site of regiments of the Commonwealth of Virginia to commemorate the officers and men of Virginia which at the time of the encampment what is now the state of West Virginia. These Virginians were wintered here in 1777-1778 as a part of General George Washingtons Army in the war for American Independence. Erected by the Sons of the American Revolution of Virginia DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque, 4 x 4 x 2. DONOR & DATE - Sons of the American Revolution of Virginia, August 3, 1983. HISTORICAL DATA - Thirteen regiments from Virginia were present at Valley Forge. Virginia was second only to Massachusetts in the number of men who enlisted in the Continental Army.

title: Varnum’s Brigade Marker, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Brigade Marker-Varnum’s Brigade Continental Army Valley Forge December 19, 1777 - June 18, 1778.  Division Varnum’s Brigade Brig. General James M. Varnum Commanding lst Regiment Rhode Island Infantry Colonel Christopher Greene 2nd Regiment Rhode Island Infantry Colonel Israel Angell 4th Regiment Connecticut Infantry Colonel John Durkee 8th Regiment Connecticut Infantry Colonel John Chandler DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque, 6 x 4 x 2. DONOR & DATE - The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA - This brigade of Rhode Island and Connecticut Infantry regiments included the lst Rhode Island Regiment which contained numerous free blacks. The Brigade Commander, General Varnum, was one of the more colorful and outspoken general officers serving at Valley Forge.

title: Unknown Soldiers Monument, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Memorial Marker-Unknown Soldiers In Memory of Unknown Soldiers Buried at Valley Forge 1777 - 1778 Erected by Valley Forge Chapter Daughters of the American Revolution 1911 DESCRIPTION - Granite with decorated bronze plaque, 7 4 x 6 3. DONOR & DATE - The Valley Forge Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution, 1912. HISTORICAL DATA - Although it is estimated that between 1,500 and 3,000 troops and auxilaries died during the Valley Forge encampment, it is not known how many were buried here, since many soldiers died in hospitals far from camp. It is certain, however that a number of burials took place at or near camp, and this monument marks one of the traditional sites.

title: Sullivan’s Bridge Site Marker, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Site Marker-Sullivan’s Bridge The Site of General Sullivan’s Bridge Erected by The American Army 1777-1778 Destroyed by Freshets in the winter of 1778-1779 this stone is erected by the Historical Society of Montgomery County Pennsylvania DESCRIPTION - Carved granite. DONOR & DATE - The Historical Society of Montgomery County, 1907. HISTORICAL DATA - In 1840 Riverboatmen took up a collection to replace a deteriorating red sandstone tablet that marked the spot where General Sullivan and his men built a bridge across the Schuylkill. The 1840 marker was of white marble but was ultimately destroyed by flood waters and replaced in 1907 by the present monument.

title: Baron von Steuben Statute, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Statue - Baron von Steuben Stonework Major General Friedrich Wilhelm Baron von Steuben Bronze Bas-relief General von Steuben Drilling Washingtons Army at Valley Forge Stonework Erected by the National German American Alliance 1915 DESCRIPTION - Bronze statue, signed J. Otto Schweizer S C, with Granite base and bronze bas-relief. DONOR & DATE - National German American Alliance, October 9, 1915. HISTORICAL DATA - The statue of von Steuben is one of only two statues in the park of the generals who served at Valley Forge. General von Steubens statue overlooks the Grand Parade Ground where he trained the soldiers of the Continental Army in the finer points of marching and maneuvering.

title: Revolutionary War Soldier Memorial Marker, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Memorial Marker-Revolutionary War Soldier Here lie the remains of a Revolutionary Soldier shot on a neighboring farm during the winter of 1777-1778. DESCRIPTION - Carved marble, 20 x 16 x 9. DONOR & DATE - Daughters of the American Revolution, pre-1902. HISTORICAL DATA - According to local tradition the soldier was shot by Devault Beaver when he caught him milking a cow on his farm. The farm was located N.E. of the Havard property, Knox Quarters, and Maxwells Quarters, the John Brown Property.

John Patton, Raised January 11, 1777 Consolidated with 11th Regiment Infantry January 13, 1779 4th Virginia Infantry 8th Virginia Infantry Colonel Abraham Bowman 12th Virginia Infantry Virginia Regiment Infantry at Large Colonel William Grayson DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque, 6 x 4 x 2. DONOR & DATE - The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA - Among other engagements in which General Scott took part was the Battle of Monmouth following the British evacuation of Philadelphia in June, 1778.

title: Rhode Island State Marker, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: State Marker-Rhode Island Dedicated Major General Nathaniel Greene Brigadier General James Mitchell Varnum Colonel Christopher Greene Colonel Israel Angell And to other officers and men of lst and 2nd Rhode Island Regiments encamped at Valley Forge in 1777-1778 -Let our name stand fair- Erected by Washington County Pomona Grange No. 2 Rhode Island DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque, 3 4 x 3 9 x 1 6. DONOR & DATE - Washington County Pomona Grange No. 2, Rhode Island, 1963. HISTORICAL DATA - The lst and 2nd Rhode Island Regiments were a part of General Varnums Brigade and the lst Rhode Island Regiment is interesting as being one of the Continental contingents which contained numerous free blacks.

title: Poor’s Brigade Marker, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Brigade Marker-Poor’s-Brigade Continental Army Valley Forge Dec. 19, 1777 June 18, 1778  Division Poor’s Brigade Brig. General Enoch Poor Commanding 1st Regiment New Hampshire Infantry Col. Joseph Cilley 2nd Regiment New Hampshire Infantry Col. Nathan Hale 3rd Regiment New Hampshire Infantry Col. Alexander Scammell 2nd Regiment New York Infantry Col. Philip Cortlandt 4th Regiment New York Infantry Col. Henry Livingston DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque 6 x 4 x 2. HISTORICAL DATA - All of the New York and New Hampshire troops at Valley Forge served under Brig. General Enoch Poor of New Hampshire. It is not presently known in which division this brigade served.

title: Pennsylvania Columns, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: East, front - Josiah Harmer Lieutenant Colonel Thomas Mifflin Major General East, back - Arthur St. Clair Major General John Cadwalader Brigadier General West, front - John J. Armstrong Brigadier General Peter G. Muhlenberg Brigadier General West, back - William Irvine Colonel 6th Penna Battalion Joseph Reed Adjutant General DESCRIPTION - Granite columns crowned with bronze eagles and bronze bas reliefs of Pennsylvania officers. DONOR & DATE - Columns - The State Legislature of Pennsylvania, June 20, 1908. Bronze bas reliefs by H.K. Bush-Brown, 1910. HISTORICAL DATA - Marks the location of the Pennsylvania line at Valley Forge under the leadership of Pennsylvanias own Brigadier General Anthony Wayne whose ancestral home is nearby at Waynesborough, Wayne, Pennsylvania.

description: Brigade Marker Patterson’s Brigade Continental Army Valley Forge December 19, 1777 June 19, 1778 Baron de Kalb’s Division Major General Baron de Kalb Patterson’s Brigade Commanding 10th Massachusetts Infantry Col. Thomas Marshal 11th Massachusetts Infantry Col. Benjamin Tupper 12th Massachusetts Infantry Col. Samuel Brewer 14th Massachusetts Infantry Col. Gamaliel Bradford DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque 6’ x 4’ x 2’. DONOR & DATE - The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the. Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA - There were four regiments in the brigade commanded by Brigadier General John Patterson in Major General Johann de Kalb’s division.

title: Pennsylvania Brigade Marker, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Brigade Marker-Pennsylvania Brigade Continental Army Valley Forge December 19, 1777 June 18, 1778 Stirlings Division Major General Lord Stirling Pennsylvania Brigade Commanding 3rd Regiment Infantry-Colonel Thomas Craig Raised January 1, 1777 mustered out November 3, 1783 6th Regiment Infantry Lieutenant Colonel Josiah Harmer Raised January 1, 1777 mustered out January 1, 1783 9th Regiment Infantry Lieutenant Colonel George Nagel Raised October 25, 1776 mustered out January, 17, 1781 12th Regiment Infantry - Colonel William Cooke Raised October 1, 1776 consolidated with 3rd Regiment Infantry July 1, 1778 DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque, 6 x 4 x 2. DONOR & DATE - The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA - Brig. General Thomas Conway had been promoted to Inspector General and left Valley Forge on December 31, 1777. This brigade however retained his name throughout the encampment.

title: North Carolina State Marker, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: State Marker-North Carolina In Memory of Nine North Carolina Regiments in Brig. Gen. Lacklan McIntoshs Brigade under General George Washington December 19, 1777- June 19, 1778 at Valley Forge Placed by the North Carolina Society NS DAR 1972 DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque, 6 x 4 x 2. DONOR & DATE - The National Society of Daughters of the American Revolution, 1972. HISTORICAL DATA - North Carolina was the 11th state to erect a monument at Valley Forge, 1972. Virginia erected a monument leaving Connecticut the only state not represented in the park.

title: New York State Marker, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: ...It is beyond description to conceive what the men suffer... Colonel Philip Van Cortlandt, Camp Valley Forge 2nd N.Y. Regiment in a letter to George Clinton Governor of New York. 13 February 1778 DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque 4 x 5 x 16. DONOR & DATE - The State of New York, 1970. HISTORICAL DATA - This marker is almost identical to the one erected for New Hampshire due to the fact that all New York and New Hampshire regiments served under the same commander at Valley Forge, Enoch Poor. Although the state of New York contributed only four regiments to the Continental Army they were generally larger than regiments from other states. New York also maintained an extensive militia on its troubled frontier. Several Loyalist units were also drawn from Southern New York.

title: New Jersey State Marker, Valley Forge Park
comment: HCS 3/19/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: State Marker-New Jersey New Jersey Brigade Continental Army Erected by The State of New Jersey upon the site occupied by the New Jersey Brigade infantry line-Continental Army Brigadier General William Maxwell First Regiment Col. Mathias Ogden Second Regiment Col Israel Shreve Third Regiment Col. Elias Dayton Fourth Regiment Col. Ephraim Martin December 19, 1777-June 18, 1778 DESCRIPTION - Marble monument topped with bronze soldier with bronze plaque. DONOR & DATE - The state of New Jersey, June 1913. HISTORICAL DATA - New Jersey was the fourth state to erect a monument to its soldiers at Valley Forge. The New Jersey troops or Jersey Blues as they were called were some of the staunchest soldiers of the Continental Army and apparently were exceedingly well organized and disciplined.

title: Muhlenberg’s Brigade Marker
comment: HCS 3/21/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Brigade Marker - Muhlenberg’s Brigade Continental Army - Valley Forge., December 19, 1777 - June 19, 1778 Greene’s Division Major General Nathaniel Greene Muhlenberg’s Brigade Brigadier General J. Peter Muhlenberg Commanding German Regiment Pennsylvania Line Lieut. Col. Lewis Weltner, raised July 12, 1776 - mustered out January 1781, 1st Regiment Virginia Infantry Colonel Richard Parker 5th Regiment Virginia Infantry Colonel Abraham Buford 9th Regiment Virginia Infantry Liet. Col. Burgess, Ball 13th Regiment Virginia Infantry Virginia State Regiment of Infantry Col. George Gibson DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque, 6’ x 4’ x 2’ DONOR & DATE - The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908 HISTORICAL DATA - With respect to the particular monument, General J. Peter Muhlenberg of Pennsylvania commanded a brigade in General Greene’s Division, made up exclusively of regiments from Virginia, with the exception on the German Regiment. composed of Pennsylvania German rank and file.

title: New Hampshire State Marker
comment: HCS 3/21/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: New Hampshire Appeal to Hon. Meshech Weare, Chief State Official Valley Forge January 21, 1778 ...Duty obligates me to observe to you the present situation of your soldiers ... Paint to yourself, this their ragged suffering condition... they lookup to me for relief, and it is not in my power to affort them any... From Enoch Poor, Brig. Gen1. Commanding New Hampshire Forces, Erected by the State of New Hampshire, DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque, 4’ x 5’ x 16”. DONOR & DATE - The State of New Hampshire, 1970. HISTORICAL DATA - The three New Hampshire regiments at Valley Forge, the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Regiments, suffered dearly at the encampment due to the distance between them and their source of supply and they were plagued with severe shortages throughout the winter.

title: McIntosh’s Brigade Marker
comment: HCS 3/21/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Brigade Marker-McIntosh’s Brigade Continental Array Valley Forge December 19, 1777 June 18, 1778 Sullivan’s Division Major General John Sullivan McIntosh’s Brigade Brig. General Lachlan McIntosh commanding 1st North Carolina Infantry Colonel Thomas Clark 2nd North Carolina Infantry Colonel John Patton 3rd North Carolina Infantry Colonel Jethro Sumner 4th North Carolina Infantry Colonel Thomas Polk 5th North Carolina Infantry Lieut. Col. William L. Davidson 6th North Carolina Infantry Colonel Gideon Lamb 7th North Carolina Infantry Colonel James Hogun 8th North Carolina Infantry Colonel James Armstrong 9th North Carolina Infantry Colonel John Williams DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque 6’ x 4’ x 2’. DONOR & DATE - The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA - The North Carolina troops at Valley Forge fared poorly because of the distance supplies from their state had to travel. They were also unaccustomed to the northern winters and seemed to suffer more because of it.

title: Brigadier General McIntosh Memorial Marker
comment: HCS 3/21/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Memorial Marker-Brigadier General McIntosh HIGH COURT TO BRIGADIER GENERAL LACHLAN MCINTOSH A GENERAL CHARGED WITH THE SAFETY OF GEORGE WASHINGTON, THE COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF OF THE CONTINENTAL ARMY AT VALLEY FORGE 1777-1778 A NATIVE OF GEORGIA IN COMMAND OF THE LIFE GUARD VIRGINIANS AND THE NORTH CAROLINA BRIGADE HIS MODEL UNIT WAS THE NUCLEUS OF FREDRICH VON STEUBENS DRILL CORPS. DEDICATED BY PATRIOTIC ORDER SONS OF AMERICA 1968 DESCRIPTION - Monument is a bronze plaque set in concrete flagpole. Size is 32’ x 16’. DONOR & DATE - Patriotic Order Sons of America, 1968. HISTORICAL DATA - It is believed that General McIntosh served as Commander of General Washingtons  Life Guards and his unit became the nucleus of the drill corps trained directly by General Von Steuben, later carrying the drill to the other units in camp.

title: Maxwell’s Brigade Marker
description: Brigade Marker-Maxwell’s Brigade Continental Army Valley Forge December 19, 1777 June 18, 1778 Sullivan’s Division Major General John Sullivan Maxwell’s Brigade Brig. Gen. William Maxwell Commanding 1st New Jersey Infantry 2nd New Jersey Infantry 3rd New Jersey Infantry 4th New Jersey Infantry DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque, 6’ x 4’ x 2’. DONOR & DATE - The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA - Maxwell’s Brigade which was part of Sullivan’s Division, consisted solely of New Jersey regiments. With Lachlan McIntosh’s Brigade, also of Sullivan’s Division, Maxwell was deployed as the defense along the linear works on the eastern face of Mt. Joy.

title: Massachusett’s State Marker
comment: HCS 3/21/2023. Original image available at this link
description: This Monument is erected by a grateful Commonwealth In memory of the soldiers of Massachusetts who served at Valley Forge. 19 Dec. 1777 ... 19 June 1778 West Elevation - Ense Petit Placidarm Sub Libertate Quietum End Pillars - 1777 1778 East Elevation - List of Massachusetts soldiers who served at Valley Forge DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque, 3’ 8” x 73’ 8”. DONOR & DATE - The Commonwealth of Massachusetts June 19, 1911. HISTORICAL DATA - Massachusetts was the third state to erect a monument, after Maine and Pennsylvania, to its men who served here at Valley Forge. Massachusetts contributed more men to the Revolution than any other colony. They came from not only the present state of Massachusetts but also from the northern frontier, Maine, and the western frontier, Vermont. Eleven regiments from Massachusetts were at Valley Forge.

title: Maryland State Marker
comment: HCS 3/21/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: State Marker - Maryland TO MARYLANDERS WHO SERVED HERE Col. Tench Tilghman, Confidential aide to Washington, who wrote formerly of my family - in every action, of, the main army often refused his pay left as fair reputation as ever belonged to human character - The Two Maryland Brigades Major General John Sullivan 1st Reg. Col. Job. H. Stone 2nd Reg. Col. Thomas Price 3rd Reg. Col. Mordecai Gist 4th Reg. Col. Josiah G. Hall Brig. General William Smallwood 5th Reg. Col. William Richardson 6th Reg. Col. Otho H. Williams 7th Reg. Col. John Gunby Reg. of Col. Moses Hazen Artillery - Captain Wm. Browns Co. and Capt. Richard Dorseys Co. and as Washington wrote, - The men- without clothes to cover their nakedness - blankets to lie upon - without shoes - their marches traced by blood from their feet - through frost and snow - without house or hut - or provisions - submitting without murmur- for the freedom of you who read this. Erected by The Maryland Society of Pennsylvania 1963 DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque, 5’ x 2’ x 1’ 1/2. DONOR & DATE - The Maryland Society of Pennsylvania, 1963. HISTORICAL DATA - The Marylanders were a part of Sullivan’s and Smallwood’s brigades. Most of the Maryland troops, however, were assigned to a location near Wilmington, Delaware for the encampment period, maintaining a Continental presence in Delaware. Some served in Patton’s additional Continental Regiment.

title: Washington’s Marquee Marker
comment: HCS 3/21/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Site Marker - Washington’s Marquee Site of the Marquee On this spot General George Washington erected his campaign tent, marquee, when he entered Valley Forge December 19, 1777. He occupied this tent until December 24, 1777 when he moved his headquarters to the Potts house at the junction of Valley Creek and Schuylkill River. DESCRIPTION - Carved granite monument. DONOR & DATE - The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1947. HISTORICAL DATA - The marker designates the traditional site where General Washington pitched his marquee for use as headquarters. He used the marquee for about a week before moving into the Potts house. According to the 1943-47 Commonwealth Report, “This granite marker is set on the points of the compass facing due south and is engraved with a directional arrow circled, and revealing the Commander-in-Chiefs initials “GW” traced from one of his original surveyors drawings.”

title: Maine State Marker
comment: HCS 3/21/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: MAINE To commemorate the officers and men from that part of New England now known as the State of Maine who served in Massachusetts Regiments with Washington at Valley Forge in the winter of 1777-8 shaping the hardships there endured this memorial is erected by the State of Maine under the auspices of the Maine Society of the Sons of The American Revolution --1907-- DESCRIPTION - Brandywine granite with bronze plaque 5’ 11’ x 5’ x 3’ 2’. DONOR & DATE - The state of Maine under the auspices of the Maine Society of the Sons of the American Revolution, 1907. HISTORICAL DATA - The state of Maine was the first state, of those who had troops at Valley Forge, to erect a monument, 1907. Maine was, at the time of the Revolution, a frontier district of Massachusetts.

title: Learned’s Brigade Marker
comment: HCS 3/21/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Brigade Marker--Learned’s Brigade Continental Army Valley Forge, December 19, 1777 - June 18, 1778 Baron de Kalb’s Division Major General Baron de Kalb Learned’s Brigade Brig. General Ebenezer Learned, Commanding 2nd Massachusetts Infantry Col. John Bailey Massachusetts Infantry Col. Michael Jackson 9th Massachusetts Infantry Col. James Wesson DESCRIPTION - Granite with bronze plaque. DONOR & DATE - The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA - Brig. General Ebenezer Learned commanded three regiments in Major General Baron Johann de Kalb’s Division - These were the 2nd, 8th, and 9th infantry regiments of the Massachusetts Line. The brigade was sometimes referred to as Late Learned’s Brigade because Learned had resigned from his command before the brigade moved to Valley Forge and it was some time before his successor was named. Learned, himself, therefore, was not at Valley Forge.

title: Huntington’s Brigade Marker, Valley Forge
comment: HCS 3/30/2023. Original image located at this link.
description: Brigade Marker-Huntington’s Brigade Continental Army Valley Forge December 19, 1777 - June 19, 1778 _________ Division Huntington’s Brigade Brig. Gen. Jedediah Huntington Commanding 1st Regiment Conn. Infantry Liet. Col. Samuel Prentice 2nd Regiment Conn. Infantry Col. Chas. Webb 5th Regiment Conn. Infantry Col. Philip B. Bradley 7th Regiment Conn. Infantry Col.. Hemen Swift DESCRIPTION: Granite with bronze plaque, 6’ x 4’ x 2’. DONOR & DATE: The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA: Huntington appears to have been one of the more dedicated Generals during this period, but he was away from Valley Forge during April of 1778. General Huntington with his four and Varnum with two Connecticut Regiments plus the 1st and 2nd Rhode Island shared the responsibility of defending the Eastern flank of the camp along the Schuylkill River.

title: Horseshoe Trail Site Marker, Valley Forge
comment: HCS 3/30/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Site Marker--Horseshoe Trail Start of the Horse-shoe Trail in Pennsylvania, Valley Forge to the Appalachian Trail on Stony Mountain 121 miles through Chester, Berks, Lancaster, Lebanon, Dauphin Counties. This marker erected 1972 by the Horse-shoe Trail Club, Inc. 1935 In memory of Henry N. Woolman, Founder DESCRIPTION: Granite, 3’ x 3’ x 3’. DONOR & DATE: The Horse-shoe Trail Club, Inc., 1972.

title: Hartley’s Brigade Marker, Valley Forge
comment: HCS 3/30/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Brigade Marker--Hartley’s Brigade Continental Army Valley Forge December 19, 1777 June 18, 1778 Pennsylvania Division Brigadier General Anthony Wayne First Brigade Colonel Thomas Hartley Commanding lst Regiment Infantry--Colonel James Chambers Raised July 1, 1776 mustered out November 3, 1783 2nd Regiment Infantry--Colonel Henry Bicker Raised October 25, 1776 mustered out November 3, 1785 7th Regiment Infantry Lieutenant Colonel David Grier Raised January 1, 1777 mustered out January 17, 1781 10th Regiment Infantry Lieutenant Colonel Adam Hubley Raised October 25, 1776 mustered out January 17, 1781 Hartley’s additional Regiment of Infantry Lieutenant Colonel Morgan Connor Raised January 11, 1777 consolidated with 11th Regiment Infantry 13, 1779 DESCRIPTION: Granite with bronze plaque, 6’ x 4’ x 2’. DONOR & DATE: The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA: The accuracy of the inscription on this monument is under question: there is doubt that Colonel Thomas Hartley was in command of the 1st Brigade of the Pennsylvania Line.

title: Glovers Brigade Marker, Valley Forge
comment: HCS 3/30/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Brigade Marker--Glover’s-Brigade Continental Army Valley Forge Dec. 19, 1777 June 18, 1778 Division Glover’s Brigade Brig. General John Glover. Commanding 1st Massachusetts Infantry Col. Joseph Vose 4th Massachusetts Infantry Col. William Shepard 13th Massachusetts Infantry Col. Edward Wigglesworth 15th Massachusetts Infantry Col. Timothy Bigelow DESCRIPTION: Granite with iron plaque, 6’ x 4’ x 2’. DONOR & DATE: The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA: John Glover of Massachusetts had commanded the famous “Marblehead Regiment” the 19th Continental Regiment, which ferried Washington’s troops across the Delaware prior to the Battle of Trenton. By late 1777, he had been elevated to Brig. General and commanded a brigade of four Massachusetts regiments at Valley Forge.

title: Georgia State Marker, Valley Forge
comment: HCS 3/30/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: State Marker--Lachlan McIntosh, Georgia, Gen. Lachlan McIntosh 1727-1806 “an officer of great worth and merit” George Washington During the winter of Valley Forge, Gen. Lachlan McIntosh of Georgia commanded the first brigade of the Continental Amy. The Brigade which was composed of North Carolina regiments, was quartered in this area. McIntosh also commanded Washingtons Life Guard. To commemorate the service of Gen. McIntosh and of other Georgians in the young Republics critical hour of Valley Forge. The STATE OF GEORGIA has gratefully erected this memorial. DESCRIPTION: Granite with bronze plaque, 4’4“ x 3’9“ x 2’. DONOR & DATE: The state of Georgia, 1959. HISTORICAL DATA: By tradition General McIntosh is reputed to have commanded Washington ’s “Life Guards” but this is, at present, unverified.

title: Delaware State Marker, Valley Forge
comment: HCS 3/30/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: State Marker--Delaware The State of Delaware erects this marker in memory of her gallant sons who endured the hardships and privations of the memorable winter of 1777-1778 on the hills of Valley Forge DESCRIPTION: Cut Brandywine granite, 6’ x 5’ x 3’. DONOR & DATE: The State of Delaware, unveiled in ceremony October 31, 1914. HISTORICAL DATA: The Delaware Regiment - there was only one - was considered by many to be the crack regiment of the Continental Army but it did not winter at Valley. Forge. Captain Allen McLane’s Regiment, however, served throughout the winter, providing Washington with details of British movements.

title: Butler’s Brigade Marker, Valley Forge
comment: HCS 3/30/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Brigade Marker--Butler’s Brigade Continental Army Valley Forge December 19, 1777 June 18, 1778 Pennsylvania Division Brigadier General Anthony Wayne Second Brigade Lieutenant Colonel William Butler Commanding 4th Regiment Infantry Lieutenant Colonel William Butler Raised January 1, 1777 mustered out January 1, 1783 5th Regiment Infantry Colonel Francis Johnston Raised January 1, 1777 mustered out June 1, 1783 8th Regiment Infantry Colonel Daniel Brodhead Raised July 20, 1776 mustered out January 17, 1781 11th Regiment Infantry Colonel Richard Hampton Raised October 25, 1776 Consolidated with 10th Regiment Infantry June 24, 1778 DESCRIPTION: Granite with bronze plaque, 6’ x 4’ x 2’. DONOR & DATE: The Valley Forge Park Commission under the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1908. HISTORICAL DATA: The 1st and 2nd Brigades of the Pennsylvania line were both encamped at this location. Anthony Wayne commanded these two brigades which constituted a Division, an unusual responsibility for a Brigadier General, but Pennsylvania’s senior officer, Arthur D. Clair had been removed from this command at this time was awaiting court martial throughout the winter of 1777-1778. There is a question as to whether or not Lieutenant Colonel William Butler was in command of the 2nd Brigade.

title: Major General Armstrong Memorial Marker, Valley Forge
comment: HCS 3/30/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Memorial Marker--Major General Armstrong Major General John Armstrong In Command of the Pennsylvania Militia Guarded the Roads from Philadelphia And the Approaches to Sullivan’s Bridge And the Camp DESCRIPTION: Pale gray granite monolith, rough-hewn on top surface and three sides. Front face a band across the foot of the monument is rough hewn to a height of 14“, the remainder is a background to the plaque. Size: 54“ x 26“ x 78“ high. DONOR & DATE: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, 1914. HISTORICAL DATA: General Armstrong, crusty commander of the Pennsylvania Militia was a veteran of the Indian Wars and was known as the “Hero of Kittanning” for his exploits on the Pennsylvania frontier routing Indians from their village bearing that name. Some Pennsylvania militia were present at the encampment and their duty was to guard the roads from Philadelphia and the northeast approaches to Sullivan’s Bridge.

title: Betsy Ross Memorial Marker, Valley Forge
comment: HCS 3/30/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Memorial Marker--Betsy Ross Betsy Ross To Honor the Maker of the First American Flag Erected 1923 Elizabeth Griscom ROSS Ashbourne Claypole 1752 1836 TRIBUTE OF PATRIOTIC ORDER SONS OF AMERICA DESCRIPTION: Dressed light gray granite consisting of an upright shaft with an eyelid-shaped curve to its upper surface; mounted on a similar base. Overall size 35“ x 17“ x 48“ high. DONOR & DATE: Patriotic Order Sons of America 1923. Originally erected at Mount Moriah Cemetery in Philadelphia by Patriotic Order Sons of America in 1923. Moved on December 17, 1975 to its present location. HISTORICAL DATA: Originally erected by the Patriotic Order Sons of America at the gravesite of Betsy Ross in the Mount Moriah Cemetery in Philadelphia in 1923. In 1975 the grave of Betsy Ross and her husband were moved to the Ross House. The Patriotic Order Sons of America monument was then moved to its Headquarters and set near the flag staff.

title: African American Monument, Valley Forge
comment: HCS 3/30/2023. Original image available at this link.
description: Memorial Marker--Patriots of African Descent IN HONOR OF PATRIOTS OF AFRICAN DESCENT WHO SERVED SUFFERED AND SACRIFICED DURING THE VALLEY FORGE ENCAMPMENT 1777 - 1778 “THROUGHOUT THESE HISTORIC AND HALLOWED CAMPSITES WERE COURAGEOUS BLACK PATRIOTS WHO PARTICIPATED IN OUR NATIONS BITTER FIGHT FOR INDEPENDENCE” CHARLES L. BLOCKSON, HISTORIAN DEDICATED BY DELTA SIGMA THETA SORORITY, INCORPORATED VALLEY FORGE ALUMNI CHAPTER JUNE 19, 1993.
